name: Comfy Image - WordPress ComfyUI Integration
summary: A WordPress plugin that enables Gutenberg users to generate and insert images using a remote ComfyUI instance via slash commands or a block widget.
goals: Let editors generate images on-the-fly inside Gutenberg using ComfyUI
Expose a slash command `/comfy` and a Gutenberg block to create images from text prompts
Provide an admin UI to configure ComfyUI endpoint, workflow templates and media options
Optionally save generated images to the WP Media Library and insert them into posts/pages
primary_features: Slash-command prompt: `/comfy <description>` inside Gutenberg to call ComfyUI
Gutenberg block: dedicated UI for prompt + advanced settings (seed, steps, model)
Admin settings page to set ComfyUI URL, default workflow, and save-to-media behavior
Server-side proxy endpoints that upload images to ComfyUI, submit workflows, poll for completion, and import results
Client-side UX: upload preview, progress updates, and image insertion into post content
secondary_features: Multiple workflow templates (shop, hero images, avatars, etc.)
CORS and host allowlist for ComfyUI integration
Admin usage logs and generated-image audit

tech_stack.comfyui: ComfyUI HTTP API (upload, prompt, history, view)

comfyui_integration.notes: Workflows are JSON objects; the plugin will ship example templates under templates/ (from image-image-gen).

security_considerations: Sanitize all inputs (sanitize_text_field, esc_url_raw) and validate remote responses
Restrict ComfyUI host via admin settings and optionally an allowlist
When saving images to media, verify MIME and use WordPress upload APIs

development_state.notes: We have example frontend ComfyUI integration (image-image-gen) and example WP admin patterns (LLM_Auto_Redirect) which will be adapted.

todo.title: Build Gutenberg block and slash command
Implement image UI and media handling
Write tests, docs and package plugin

requirements: WordPress development environment (LocalWP, Docker, or WP-CLI)
ComfyUI instance accessible from the host running WordPress
steps: Copy the plugin folder into wp-content/plugins/comfy-image
Activate the plugin in WP Admin > Plugins
Open Settings > Comfy Image and configure ComfyUI URL
Open Gutenberg editor and add the Comfy block or type /comfy <prompt>

open_questions: Should generated images be saved to WP Media by default?
Which WordPress roles are allowed to generate images (editors/authors/contributors)?
Do we need authentication between WP and ComfyUI (API key or reverse proxy)?
Do we want server-side download into media or remote embedding by URL?
notes: This file is intentionally prescriptive to let an LLM pick up development. Follow PLAN.md for the implementation milestones.
